assessments.quote: Experiments on three benchmarks (LiTS, KiTS, and BraTS) show that M-Net achieves Dice scores of 78.42%, 76.15%, and 83.67%, outperforming baseline U-Net by 12.37%, 3.52%, and 5.55% on liver, kidney, and brain tumor segmentation, respectively.
assessments.reason: Involves liver tumor segmentation on LiTS but performs whole-lesion segmentation, not within-lesion subregion subdivision; the task constraint is violated. Methodologically relevant as a recent deep-learning segmentation approach.

assessments.quote: MRI-Glioma Net wasbuilt as a new 3D Res-UNet framework.
assessments.reason: Brain glioma subregion segmentation (WT/TC/ET), not liver tumor; population and organ mismatch. Subregion concept is brain-specific, not liver tumor subregion subdivision.

assessments.quote: The dice coefficients for the multiple branch TS-U-net model were 0.876, 0.868, and 0.814 in the tumor subregions of WT, TC, and ET, respectively.
assessments.reason: Brain tumor (BraTS) subregion segmentation, not liver tumor. Population mismatch; no liver tumor subregion evidence.

assessments.quote: this paper discusses a tumor image segmentation algorithm that combines thresholding and region-growing methods
assessments.reason: Generic tumor segmentation/classification review with thresholding and region-growing; no liver tumor subregion subdivision and no specific experimental evidence in abstract.
